html:
SMTO-FIL-0024 — This file task is too big for SMTO to do in one step

GUID: 7d81a01d-0298-4c6b-bc5b-11472f486448
Slug: file-result-limit
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The files or changes involved are larger than SMTO handles in one step, such as editing a file over 8 MB, comparing very long files, or changing more than 64 files at once. This step was stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to split the work into smaller steps, for example a few files at a time or one section of a large file at a time. Each step has a size limit, and smaller pieces stay under it.
  2. For a very large file, ask SMTO to read or change only the part you care about, such as a range of lines. Editing and comparing load the whole file, and files over 8 MB are too big for that.
  3. If SMTO was copying, moving or deleting a large or deeply nested folder, ask it to handle one subfolder at a time. SMTO checks every item before starting, and very large folders exceed how many it can check.

What success looks like

  • Each smaller step finishes, and together they cover all the work you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't accept a result that quietly leaves out part of your files; ask SMTO to confirm that every part was covered.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation exceeded a fixed bound: 1 MiB request arguments, the 8 MiB text buffer for edit/diff/patch, 20,000 aggregate diff lines, 1 MiB, 64-file or 16 MiB aggregate patch limits, 128-level mkdir or recursive depth, an incomplete recursive preflight inventory, or extended-attribute size limits.

What this means

  • A file operation exceeds a bounded input, text buffer, traversal depth, metadata, patch, edit, diff or inventory limit. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A file operation exceeds a bounded input, text buffer, traversal depth, metadata, patch, edit, diff or inventory limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation's specific size/count/depth limit; this kind is not restricted to result pagination.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt message for the bound that was hit (gateway_core/file_contract limits, file_common.load_text, file_mutate.edit/diff/mkdirs, file_patch.parse_patch/patch, file_manage.tree, file_metadata). Split the work into ranged reads, per-file edits, fewer patch targets or per-subtree recursive operations, or raise max_entries_scanned within ENTRY_LIMIT (100000).
  • Reduce the specific file, patch, metadata or traversal scope to its advertised bound without silently dropping required content.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A smaller supported operation fits its input, processing and result bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
